newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CROATIA TROUNCE BOSNIA ON NEUTRAL GROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CROATIA TROUNCE BOSNIA ON NEUTRAL GROUND.

text.p: Bosnia made their "home" World Cup debut against Croatia on Tuesday and lost 4-1.

Striker Alen Boksic, who plays for European Cup holders Juventus, scored two second half goals as Croatia repeatedly ripped through a Bosnian defence bravely shored up by veteran goalkeeper Fahrudin Omerovic.

While tempers never flared on the pitch or in the cavernously empty Renato Dell' Ara stadium, where a pitifully poor attendance left the impression of a match played behind closed doors, there was plenty of emotion.
One busload of Bosnians travelled for some 22 hours to watch their national team play in Bologna, hosting Bosnia's first home match after FIFA ruled out Sarajevo's Kosevo stadium on safety grounds.
Bosnia's first venture on to the World Cup stage ended in a 3-0 defeat in Greece last month.
But the enthusiasm of the Bosnian fans, most of whom had expected defeat, was hardly dampened as they huddled in driving rain and watched Croatia take an early lead.

Defender Slaven Bilic, who had complained of foot pain in weekend training and had doubted whether he would play, connected cleanly with a right-footed volley in the 14th minute to send the highly-fancied Croats ahead.
But Bosnia stunned their neighbours with a well-taken equaliser from Hasan Salihamidzic, who plays for Hamburg, against the run of play just 11 minutes later.
The 1-1 scoreline, which would have constituted a clear upset for the Croats whose team impressed many at Euro 96, was short lived.
Striker Goran Vlaovic, who played in Italy's serie A for Padova last season, made it 2-1 in the 32nd minute.
Boksic then scored the third by breaking free and lobbing the goalkeeper in the 63rd minute.
He added the fourth in the 84th by dribbling past a defender and curling in a right-footed shot from the edge of the area.

Bosnia - 1-Fahrudin Omerovic, 2-Nermin Sabic (17-Senad Begic, 53rd), 3-Bakir Besirevic, 4-Muhamed Konjic (16-Sanin Pintul, 69th), 5-Sunad Katana, 6-Nudzein Geca, 7-Admir Smajic, 8-Mehmed Bazdarevic, 9-Elvir Bolic, 10-Amir Teljigovic (18-Halilovic 62nd), 11-Hasan Salihamidzic
